why: A lamp at c lights exactly the objects inside a segment of length 2*radius, so the question is the maximum number of sorted points fitting in a window of width 2*radius. Two pointers slide that window over the sorted coordinates; for the first best window ending at objects[j], the smallest lamp spot is objects[j] - radius.
hints: Instead of trying every coordinate c, think about which groups of objects can be lit together. What must be true of the leftmost and rightmost lit objects?
A set of consecutive objects objects[i..j] can be lit together iff objects[j] - objects[i] <= 2 * radius. Find the largest such window with two pointers.

Grow j, shrink i while the span exceeds 2r, and on a strictly larger count record c = objects[j] - radius (the leftmost lamp that still reaches objects[j]). Strict improvement keeps the smallest c. O(n).
pitfalls: The answer is a lamp coordinate, not a count or an object.
Lamp positions are not limited to object coordinates; the smallest valid c is objects[j] - radius, which can be negative (example 3 returns 4 for object 7).
Only update on a strictly larger count, otherwise you drift to a larger coordinate for the same count.
